U1, U2, U4, U5, U6		Place a 100 nF capacitor within 5 mm of every power pin (plus bulk capacitance per rail).

1 · Build the test fixture

Fixture PCB with pogo pins (render of the generated .kicad_pcb)
Probe points on the board (red = supply, dark = GND, green = measured)

Parts

  • 14 x pogo pin P75 (14 crown tip)
  • 14 x receptacle R75 (fixture drill 1.40 mm)
  • 0805 resistors: 4 x 1200 ohm, 4 x 10000 ohm, 7 x 12000 ohm, 7 x 100000 ohm
  • 1 x 2 x 7 pin header 2.54 mm, 1 x 2-pin 5.08 mm terminal block
  • guide pins matching the board's mounting holes; 4 x M3 standoffs
1
Open pic_programmer-fixture.kicad_pcb in KiCad, route the ratsnest (or run Freerouting), run DRC and order the PCB.
2
Press the receptacles into the plated holes and solder them; insert the pogo pins (crown tips on through-hole leads, spear tips on flat pads - see the probes CSV).
3
Fit the guide pins in the GUIDE holes; they locate the board through its mounting holes. Mount the fixture on M3 standoffs.
4
Solder the divider resistors, header and power terminal. Wire the header to the measurement hardware as shown below.

Wiring

2 · Run a production test

Lower the board onto the guide pins...
...and press it down: every pogo pin touches its test point
1
Copy the runner folder to the Raspberry Pi and describe your wiring in hardware.json.
2
Once, with known-good boards: python3 pcbtest_runner.py learn --units 3 to fill in signal limits.
3
For every board: place it, press down, run python3 pcbtest_runner.py test --loop and enter the serial number.
4
Green PASS: next board. Red FAIL: the failed checks are listed and stored in results/results.csv.
StepWhat is checked
S1 Visual inspectionPolarity/orientation correct, IC pin-1 orientation matches silkscreen, Through-hole joints filled, leads clipped <= 1.5 mm
S2 Unpowered short check (rails to GND)VCC_PIC 100.0.., VPP{slash}MCLR 100.0.., VCC 100.0.., VPP 100.0..
S3 Apply power (/pic_sockets/VCC_PIC = None V)VCC_PIC None..None
S4 Rail voltagesVPP{slash}MCLR None..None, VCC None..None, VPP None..None
S5 Signal levels (idle)PC-DATA-IN None..None, Net-(D1-A) None..None, PC-CLOCK-OUT None..None, PC-DATA-OUT None..None, VPP_ON None..None, CLOCK-RB6 None..None
S9 Remove power

3 · Hand-solder with the jigs

3D-printed jig (167.25 x 123.25 x 17.74 mm)
place part hereclearance for assembled partsalignment post

Print pic_programmer-jig.stl as it is (pockets face up, no supports): PLA or PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 3 walls. The pocket map is the jig as it lies on your desk.

Placement jig (172.25 x 111.25 x 13.4 mm): lead wells, post holes and locating stops
1
Print both jigs as they are (no supports): pic_programmer-jig-placement.stl (placement jig) and pic_programmer-jig.stl (holding jig).
2
Put the PCB top side up into the placement jig; the stops around the edge locate it.
3
Fit the hand-soldered parts: C1 (100µF), C2 (220uF), C3 (22uF/25V), C4 (0), C5 (10nF), C6 (100nF), C7 (100nF), C9 (220nF), D1 (1N4004), D2 (BAT43), D3 (BAT43), D4 (BAT43), D5 (BAT43), D6 (BAT43), D7 (BAT43), D8 (RED-LED), D9 (GREEN-LED), D10 (SCHOTTKY), D11 (BAT43), D12 (YELLOW-LED), L1 (22uH), P1 (CONN_2), P2 (SUPP28), P3 (SUPP40), Q1 (BC237), Q2 (BC307), Q3 (BC307), R1 (10K), R2 (10K), R3 (10K), R4 (10K), R5 (10K), R6 (10K), R7 (10K), R8 (1K), R9 (2.2K), R10 (5,1K), R11 (22K), R12 (470), R13 (470), R14 (470), R15 (6.2K), R16 (62K), R17 (22K), R18 (220), R19 (2.2K), R20 (2.2K), R21 (470), RV1 (1K), U1 (24Cxx), U2 (74HC125), U3 (7805), U4 (LT1373), U5 (PIC_18_PINS), U6 (PIC_8_PINS). Mind polarity marks. The leads go into the wells under the board; trim leads longer than 10 mm.
4
Put the holding jig on top, pockets down: its posts go through the mounting holes and every part sits in its pocket.
5
Hold both jigs together and turn the stack over. Lift off the placement jig: every lead now points up.
6
Solder all leads from above, clip them, lift the board out with the finger notches.
Parts in their pockets, PCB coming down (top side facing the jig)
PCB seated: solder from above
